capture_cost.decode_step_reference_ms: a 1.5B-parameter decode step on an H100 is ~10-20 ms at this batch (order of magnitude, not measured here)
capture_cost.note: rate 1/4 code as the proofs use; n=8192 halves every line; the Brakedown line is the gather-bound expander at 0.092 utilisation

in_circuit_sha256.sees: roots (in O) and the verdict; the leaf bytes and digests stay inside the proof
in_circuit_sha256.simulatable_because: no new prover message: the hash constraints are checker constraints and inherit the design's HVZK/step-0 argument
in_circuit_sha256.assumption: none beyond the design's (CRH of H); no hiding assumption on SHA-256 since digests are never disclosed

verifier_openings.sees: the opened leaves in the clear: x rows, W rows, whole output rows
verifier_openings.simulatable_because: n/a -- acceptable only for tensors that are public by policy (open-weights models: W); never for activations

leaf_v2_pcs_hash.sees: the tensor digest (Poseidon2 Merkle root over salted row leaves), the SHA-256 ids path, the verdict
leaf_v2_pcs_hash.simulatable_because: row leaves are H(row || salt) with a fresh 31-bit x 8 salt: a hiding commitment under Poseidon2 as a (pseudo)random function; the digest is then independent of the rows; the in-circuit part inherits the design's ZK
leaf_v2_pcs_hash.assumption: hiding of salted Poseidon2 (beyond CRH): an extra assumption to state; salt per row must be fresh per commitment

algebraic.sees: t opened columns of every touched chunk, two blinded combination polynomials (v: degree < k, q: degree < 2k-1), the chunk roots, the verdict
algebraic.simulatable_because: t <= k - l columns of rows with fresh randomizers are uniform (Ligero Lemma 4.15); v and q are one-time-padded by the proof's blinding rows; Q and the coefficients are committed at step 0 (HM96), so a malicious verifier gains nothing from adaptivity; the ids-tree path is over digests only
algebraic.assumption: the randomizer budget: the SUM of t over every opening of one commitment must stay <= k - l (weights re-randomised per session or public; l chosen for the number of proofs per runtime commitment); HM96 binding for step 0 as in ZK_CONSTRUCTION.md

breakthrough_criterion.rule: a viable private option within 20% of the numerical-only (non-ZK, auth excluded) number

citations.sha256_lookup_air: T. Coratger, 'SHA-256 AIR for Stwo' design note (hackmd.io/@tcoratger/HJFGugU0Ze, read 2026-09-22): lookup-based M31 layout, schedule 48 x (22 trace + 8 lookups) + compression 64 x (52 trace + 21 lookups) = 4 384 trace cells + 1 728 LogUp interactions ~ 7 840 cells per compression (L counted as 2T).
citations.sha256_p3_air: Plonky3 p3-sha256-air 0.7.0-rc.1 (docs.rs, read 2026-09-22): one compression per row, 7 488 columns, bit-decomposed sigma/Ch/Maj, packed 16-bit-limb additions, max constraint degree 3, no lookups.
citations.sha256_r1cs: faulhornlabs/hash-circuits README (read 2026-09-21): SHA-256 two-to-one compression 26 170 nonlinear R1CS constraints; circomlib Sha256(256) 29 380 (RareSkills circom tutorial). https://github.com/faulhornlabs/hash-circuits
citations.sp1_sha_air: sp1-core ShaCompressChip docs: 'each SHA compress syscall takes up 80 rows' (8 init, 64 compression, 8 finalize). https://docs.rs/sp1-core/latest/sp1_core/syscall/precompiles/sha256/struct.ShaCompressChip.html
citations.poseidon2_babybear: Plonky3 p3-baby-bear poseidon2.rs (read 2026-09-22): BabyBear Poseidon2 S-box x^7, R_F = 8, R_P = 13 (width 16) / 21 (width 24); hash-gpu lane's fused CUDA kernel matches Plonky3's test vectors (reports/hash_gpu.md).
citations.hash_gpu: backends/numerical/reports/hash_gpu.md, run r20260922-054241-b966 (RTX 4090): full-tree SHA-256 446 GB/s (B shape), Blake3 359 GB/s, Poseidon2/BabyBear w16 57.7 GB/s, w24 34.2 GB/s; generic 32 B-leaf trees SHA-256 146 GB/s.
citations.ligero_zk: Ames-Hazay-Ishai-Venkitasubramaniam, Ligero (ePrint 2022/1608) Lemma 4.15: with k - l randomizers per row any t <= k - l opened columns are uniform; the linear/quadratic test responses are hidden by one blinding row each.
citations.leaf_v1: packages/verity/src/verity/commitments/leaves.py: H(tag,*parts)=sha256(u32be(len tag)||tag||(u64be(len part)||part)*); leaf=(id,dtype,shape,value); node/lift; DIGEST_BYTES=32; path_shape/tree_depth.
citations.bench_sharing: fixtures/bench-instances/v1/vu-k1536.index.json + seeds/seeds.json: 3 456 real VUs = 24 seeds x 144 weight rows; 2 598 distinct (op, j) weight rows over 18 weight matrices; 640 corners with their own operands.
citations.tensor_model: backends/numerical/reports/tensor.md (explore.tensor): H100 INT8 dense 989.5 T MAC/s x utilisation 0.172; RS n=16384/k=4096 as a two-stage matrix DFT: 4096 x 128 + 16384 x 256 base MACs per row (x L^2 = 16 limb MACs on BabyBear).

assumptions: in-circuit SHA-256 priced as the Stwo-style lookup AIR (7 840 cells / compression; 4 384 constraints + 1 728 lookups) and the R1CS circuit (26 170) as bracket; a cell is one sumcheck element (A) / one committed element (B)
Poseidon2/BabyBear: 4 multiplications per x^7 S-box, one linear wire per state element per round; rate = width/2 words (one 16-bit word per element); salt 8 elements per row leaf
algebraic: two row combinations + one size-n interpolant per touched tensor row (matrix-DFT price), t=191 columns of every touched chunk of R=64 rows opened; verifier folds them natively
bench sharing = the frozen instance set's real structure scaled to 4 096 real VUs; decode_step and worst bracket it
leaf_v2_pcs_hash rows-per-tensor for the row tree: 256 tokens (activations), 2 048 rows (weights): assumptions
weights_public: W rows opened to the verifier under leaf/v1 and pinned by public linear constraints (no privacy for W by policy)
